questions.q: A relation R on set A is called reflexive if:
options: (a, b) in R implies (b, a) in R
(a, a) in R for all a in A
(a, b) in R and (b, c) in R implies (a, c) in R
questions.explanation: Reflexive means every single element in the domain is related to itself.

questions.q: The range of the function f(x) = |x| is:
questions.explanation: Absolute value is always non-negative, meaning the range is [0, infinity).

questions.q: An equivalence relation partitions a set into:
questions.explanation: Equivalence classes are mutually disjoint and their union covers the original set.

questions.q: If f(x) = x<sup class="sup">2</sup> and g(x) = x + 1, what is f(g(x))?
questions.explanation: Substitute g(x) into f: f(x+1) = (x+1)<sup class="sup">2</sup>.

questions.q: Is the relation 'is less than' (<) on Real numbers symmetric?
questions.explanation: If 2 < 3, it is NOT true that 3 < 2. So it is not symmetric.

questions.q: A function f: A -> B is invertible if and only if it is:
questions.explanation: Only bijective functions have well-defined inverses because every output maps back to a single unique input.
